author: William Wordsworth
title: The Poetical Works of William Wordsworth, Volume II
edition: Edited by William Knight, volume II,1896, as explicitly identified in the Project Gutenberg12145 front matter. Poem text extracted from the HTML tables’ text column; separate variant, footnote and line-number columns, navigation links and editorial commentary are outside the selected poems. Original punctuation, spelling, verse lines and stanza divisions retained. HTML whitespace is normalized within each verse line, with physical HTML wraps distinguished from br verse boundaries. No text rewritten.

rights.basis: The identified English edition edited by William Knight was published in1896, before1931; its US copyright term has expired as of2026. Project Gutenberg12145 explicitly marks the work public domain in the USA. Original English; no translator.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg 12145 HTML from the PG mirror aleph.pglaf.org. For each poem in the volume's order: the poem title (h2, footnote letters removed) as a level-2 heading, then the text column of every table whose header row names a text column, joined row by row; br marks a verse line (HTML wrapping and indentation inside a line collapsed to single spaces), blank lines divide stanzas, stanza numerals (from a stanza column or enlarged numerals in the text) and bold part titles (Prologue, Part the First...) are level-3 headings, and year and group titles (1799, Poems on the Naming of Places...) are level-1 headings. Removed the PG header and footer, Knight's contents, notes and commentary, the Fenwick (I. F.) notes, the variant, footnote and line-number columns, footnotes, navigation links and the composed/published date lines; italics are not marked. The four bracketed note numbers printed in verse lines (blocks 638, 915, 1031 and 1085), which point to Knight’s footnotes, were removed on 2026-11-18, since the notes they refer to are not held.

scope.note: Holds the text of every poem in Knight's volume II (1798-1803) in its printed order; Knight's editorial apparatus (notes, variants, footnotes, line numbers, date lines), the Fenwick notes and the prose dedication of Peter Bell, which the edition prints among that apparatus, are not held.
